parts.text: A student investigates the resistance of a wire. Fig. 2.1 shows the circuit he uses. Fig. 2.1

parts.label: b
parts.text: (b) The student places the sliding contact 15.0 cm from B. He measures the potential difference (p.d.) V across the length d = 15.0 cm of resistance wire BC. He repeats the procedure using values of d = 40.0 cm, d = 60.0 cm and d = 80.0 cm. The values of d, V and R are shown in Table 2.1. The voltmeter reading he obtains when d = 100.0 cm is shown in Fig. 2.3.

parts.label: i
parts.text: (i) Record, in the last row of Table 2.1, the voltmeter reading shown in Fig. 2.3. [1] Fig. 2.3

parts.label: ii
parts.text: (ii) Calculate the resistance R of 100.0 cm of the resistance wire, using the equation R = V I . Record R in the last row of Table 2.1. [1]

parts.label: iii
parts.text: (iii) Complete the column headings in Table 2.1. [1] Table 2.1 d / V / R / 15.0 0.4 1.25 40.0 1.1 3.44 60.0 1.4 4.38 80.0 2.1 6.56 100.0
